translationRepairs: In the Zhenguang era Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed grand mentor.
In the Zhenguang era Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed grand commandant.
s0004 has 授普太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not grand mentor (太傅/太保). The proposed replacement corrects the office title.
In the Zhenguang era, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed Grand Mentor.
In the Zhenguang era, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Pu was appointed Grand Commandant.
The same Chinese 授普太尉 shows Grand Mentor is wrong in the literal field; Grand Commandant matches 太尉.
He rose through repeated promotions to grand mentor and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
He rose through repeated promotions to grand commandant and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
s0009 has 累遷太尉、朔州刺史; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not grand mentor. The repair restores the correct office.
He rose in repeated promotions to Grand Mentor and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
He rose in repeated promotions to Grand Commandant and inspector of Shuozhou, then died.
Literal likewise mistranslates 太尉 as Grand Mentor; Grand Commandant is the accurate title.
When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Yue.
When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Houmochen Yue.
共圖悅 targets Houmochen Yue (悅), not Heba Yue (岳). After 率岳所部, bare English 'Yue' wrongly invites reading the plot as against Heba Yue; naming Houmochen Yue removes that error.
When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Yue.
When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Yuwen Tai led Yue's troops back and together they plotted against Houmochen Yue.
The literal has the same 共圖悅 referent; specifying Houmochen Yue correctly disambiguates 悅 from 岳.
When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianzhong led the forces of Guanxi and, with Erzhu Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianguang led the forces of Guanxi and, with Erzhu Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
s0096 names 尒朱天光; 天光 is Tianguang, not Tianzhong. The replacement corrects the personal name.
When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianzhong led the forces of Guanxi and, with Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
When Gao Huan raised the righteous rising, Erzhu Tianguang led the forces of Guanxi and, with Zhongyuan and others, resisted the righteous army in the north.
The literal likewise misreads 天光 as Tianzhong; Tianguang matches the Chinese name.
Tianzhong left Zuo in Eastern Qin with overall command of three provinces and charge of pacifying two.
Tianguang left Zuo in Eastern Qin with overall command of three provinces and charge of pacifying two.
Antecedent 天光 continues Erzhu Tianguang from s0096; Tianzhong is a false reading of 天光.
Tianzhong left Zuo in Eastern Qin, with overall command of three provinces and responsibility for pacifying two provinces.
Tianguang left Zuo in Eastern Qin, with overall command of three provinces and responsibility for pacifying two provinces.
Literal 天光 must likewise be Tianguang, matching the established name in the prior unit.
When Tianzhong was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made grand general of chariots and cavalry.
When Tianguang was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made grand general of chariots and cavalry.
天光敗 again refers to Erzhu Tianguang; Tianguang corrects the misread given name.
When Tianzhong was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
When Tianguang was defeated, Zuo submitted to Gao Huan and was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
The literal 天光敗 has the same referent; Tianguang is the accurate reading of 天光.
Zican served as the commandery merit clerk and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianzhong in pacifying Guanxi.
Zican served as the commandery merit clerk and rose in succession to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, following Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guanxi.
